# One payment of INV-USD-001, made of two splits of one transaction.
#
# `txn_guid:` + `txn_split_guid:` name one settling split, which is nearly
# every settlement. This is the other case, and it is written as directives:
#
#     Transaction "<the transaction>"
#         PaymentSplit "<one split>"
#         PaymentSplit "<the other>"
#
# One `payment:` block, because this is one payment — the money arrived once.
# Written as two blocks it would read as the invoice having been paid twice,
# which is a different fact about the customer.
#
# Splits are children of the transaction they belong to, which is where a
# split lives everywhere else in this format. Directives are capitalised, so
# they read apart from the block's own lower-case keys.
#
# What this fixture produces: both parked splits become the receivable, in the
# invoice's lot, and the entry is quoted in USD with no CAD left in it.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
